Definition: from G3685; profitable; Onesimus, a Christian:--Onesimus.
BiblicalUsage: Onesimus is the runaway slave Paul sends back to Philemon, a faithful and beloved brother in Colossians 4:9, and Paul's son in the faith in Philemon 1:10, begotten in his bonds. His name means profitable, and Paul's letter turns the useless runaway into a brother.
TheologicalSignificance: I hold that Onesimus proves the gospel makes brothers of masters and slaves, and the profitable one is the one Christ has changed.
